cost: Validation O(L+E); mate initialization O(L+R). Each of L searches initializes L+R slots and visits at most L left vertices, R right vertices and E edges; flipping uses O(L+R). Total O((L+1)(L+R+E)) time and O(L+R) auxiliary space, including the L=0,R>0 allocation. No timing claim.
forward: Validate every right endpoint in left/adjacency order; return the first InvalidEdge. Otherwise return one Option<usize> per left vertex, describing an injective edge subset of maximum cardinality. Process roots by increasing left index, FIFO discovery and adjacency order. Duplicate edges and empty/unequal partitions are valid. The selected optimum is deterministic for identical input but not promised lexicographically least or invariant under edge reordering.

inverse: Let X be allocated finite ordered adjacency vectors and usize right-partition sizes, and Y the typed Result<Vec<Option<usize>>,BipartiteMatchingError> observation space, excluding allocation failure and nontermination. Define R subset X times Y by first-invalid-edge validation followed by the exact ordered FIFO augmenting traversal in Forward, not by arbitrary maximum matching. Set U=X times Y and behavior_complement=U minus R. It includes every valid maximum differing from that deterministic selected vector, as well as invalid, infeasible and submaximum observations. Finite negative fixtures check selected memberships only.

For output mate vector m, compatible inputs have L=len(m), R greater than every present mate, contain every selected edge and have matching number equal to count(Some). Exact compatibility additionally requires the stated FIFO/adjacency traversal to select m. Different edge sets and duplicate multiplicities can fit one result; unique graph recovery is not claimed. InvalidEdge restricts inputs to the reported first invalid endpoint and all earlier endpoints valid.
limitations: Partial syntax has no macro expansion or type resolution. Bounded evidence is not proof. Allocation failures are outside the Result contract. No approximate executable profiles.
